definitions.meaning: A circle split into wedges that show fractions of a whole: in the animation the whole is 12 pupils, with apples 1/2, bananas 1/4 and grapes 1/4.
Points joined by a line to show how a value changes over time: plants sold were Jan 20, Feb 35, Mar 30 and Apr 50.
Bars whose heights show amounts that can be compared: soccer 13 votes, badminton 8 votes and swimming 3 votes.
The numbers along an axis that say what the drawing stands for: graph A runs 0 to 50 while graph B runs 0 to 200.

mechanismSteps: Reading a pie chart: who likes what?: 6 of 12 pupils chose apples (1/2), and 3 each chose bananas and grapes (1/4 each).
Reading a line graph: a rising trend: plants sold climb from Jan 20 to Apr 50 overall, with a small dip to 30 in March.
Worked example: comparing two bars of data: soccer has 13 votes and badminton has 8 votes, so 13 - 8 = 5 more chose soccer.
Watch out: a steeper line is not always bigger: both shops rose from 20 to 40, a rise of +20 each, but graph B only looks flatter because its axis runs 0 to 200 instead of 0 to 50.
objectives: Read a pie chart as fractions of a whole
Read values and trends from a line graph
Compare two bars of data by subtracting their heights
Check the axis scale before comparing how steep two lines look
subject: math
title: Data graphs: pie charts and line graphs

trap.explanation: Steepness is judged by the drawing rather than the axis scale behind it. Slope depends on the axis scale: two graphs can have the same rise but look different. In the animation scene s4 both shops rose by +20, from 20 to 40, even though one line looks steeper.
trap.misconception: A steeper line always means a bigger increase.

workedExample: In scene s3, 24 children voted: the soccer bar reads 13 and the badminton bar reads 8, so 13 − 8 = 5 more chose soccer. Read the heights from the labels first, then subtract the smaller height from the bigger one.
